name: Complete Leg Weave Pass
description: Complete Leg Weave Pass clears the remaining foot or half-guard hook after the passer's arm folds the knees together. Secure chest control before settling.
summary: The leg-weave pass uses an arm threaded between the legs to bring the knees together, then clears the remaining foot or half-guard hook before settling into side control.
overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint. Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Lachlan Giles — leg weave pass, no gi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rDzchSk4fw); [Lachlan Giles — leg-weave counter demonstration](https://bjjfanatics.com/blogs/news/interesting-leg-weave-counter-with-lachlan-giles).

attacker.name: Complete Leg Weave Pass Attacker
attacker.description: Complete Leg Weave Pass (attacker): Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
attacker.overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint. Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.

Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm. Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control. If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Keep hip control as the last foot or half-guard hook clears, then settle the side pin with a supported crossface. The head and shoulder connection holds the upper body while your hip block prevents a fresh knee insertion.

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (top): What should the weaving arm connect to?
flashcards.answer: Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Through gap to lower thigh or knee

plausible: Upper shin alone, lower knee free
Under both thighs, not between them
trap: Outside both knees, missing the gap

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (top): What pressure direction reduces the shield?
flashcards.answer: Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
flashcards.answer_line: Fold upper knee toward lower knee

plausible: Lift upper knee away from lower knee
Push lower knee away, shield upright
trap: Press shin in, leave knees separated

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (top): What arm exposure invites a kimura counter?
flashcards.answer: Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.
flashcards.answer_line: Long arm, wrist and elbow exposed

plausible: Elbow connected as your base moves
A hand withdrawn during a reset
trap: Bent elbow at ribs, wrist hidden

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (top): What lets you move without tipping over the woven arm?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.
flashcards.answer_line: An outside base with hips and feet

plausible: All weight over the extended wrist
Feet crossed tight, leaning forward
trap: Knees under chest, weight past arm

flashcards.answer_line: Clear hook before settling the pin

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (top): The opponent turns their hips and adds a frame. What now?

defender.name: Complete Leg Weave Pass Defender
defender.description: Complete Leg Weave Pass (defender): The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
defender.overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together. Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.

Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs. An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned. Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Use a shoulder frame and a short shrimp to make an early escape before the last knee is passed. An underhook can recover a facing base while the shoulder is still free; keep its elbow connected if the passer counters with an overhook.
key_principles: Recognize the arm weave: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
Keep the shield supported: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
Recover inside space: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
Deny upper-body collapse: Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs.
Use an available underhook: An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned.
Move the whole leg: Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.
recognition_cues: The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame.
Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (bottom): Which control is bringing your knees together?
flashcards.answer: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.

plausible: Their arm scoops under both thighs
Palm on shin, lower knee untouched

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (bottom): Before the shield collapses, what keeps it useful?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee angle with a shoulder frame

plausible: Straight arm, elbow far from knee
Both knees folded, no upper frame
trap: Knee angle, hands below their hip

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (bottom): What creates room for the inside knee before the final clearance?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder frame and lateral hip shift

plausible: Pull head, hips beneath the passer
Grip wrist, hips beneath the passer

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (bottom): Why resist being flattened while the legs are controlled?
flashcards.answer: Preserve a shoulder frame and side angle so leg control does not become a settled upper-body pin.

plausible: Flat shoulders turn hips to recover
Ankle hook replaces shoulder space
trap: Weave stops them also pinning torso

flashcards.question: Complete Leg Weave Pass (bottom): When can an underhook help recover half guard?
flashcards.answer: An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder free to turn and face

plausible: Shoulder fully pinned without space
Elbow pinned away by their overhook
